resolver um cenário de apoio acadêmico em quatro etapas.
Imagine you're struggling in a course. Who would you ask for help at university?
Have you ever had a tutor? Was it useful?

→ writing / book a session at the writing center → chemistry / ask the TA during office hours → time management / talk to an academic coach

Free one-on-one tutoring is available for all first- and second-year students in math, statistics, chemistry and economics. Sessions last 50 minutes and must be booked online at least 24 hours in advance. Each student can book up to two sessions per week. Drop-in hours (no appointment needed) are Monday to Thursday, 4–6 p.m., in Room 210 of the Learning Commons. During midterm weeks, demand is high, so students are encouraged to book early. Students who miss two booked sessions without canceling will lose booking privileges for the rest of the semester.

Etapa 2 — Ouça (🎧 professor lê uma vez, 3 min)
Hi, you must be Alex. So, what's going on with statistics?
I'm having trouble with probability. I understood the first chapters, but now I'm lost, and the midterm is in ten days.

OK, that's very common. Here's what I suggest. Book two sessions a week with me until the midterm — that's the maximum. But also, come to drop-in hours on Wednesday. This week they're actually moving to Room 115, because 210 is being painted.
Oh, good to know. Should I bring anything?

Bring your last two homework assignments and a list of the problems you got wrong. Oh, and one more thing — talk to your professor. Professor Grant offers a practice midterm to students who ask for it by email.

content.text: Etapa 3 — Fale (4 min: 1 min de preparo + 1 min de fala, duas tentativas)
seu amigo Sam também está com dificuldade em estatística e pergunta:
“What are you going to do to prepare for the midterm?”
(sessões, drop-in, sala nova, o que levar, e-mail para a professora).
Well, I talked to a tutor at the Tutoring Center, and here's my plan…
Write an email to Professor Grant. Introduce yourself, explain your situation briefly, mention what you're doing to improve, and ask for the practice midterm.
